newsitem.title: USA: US bridge linking Va,Md needs funds boost-senators.
newsitem.headline: US bridge linking Va,Md needs funds boost-senators.

text.p: U.S. House and Senate members from Maryland and Virginia said Friday that it is urgent that the federal government commit more funds to replace the dilapidated Woodrow Wilson Bridge linking the two states.

"The London Bridge may be falling down but the Woodrow Wilson Bridge should not," Sen. Barbara Mikulski, D-Md., said at a hearing by the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee's subpanel on transportation.
"Design estimates indicate it would cost $1.6 billion to replace the bridge," Mikulski said. "The (Clinton) Administration budget for fiscal year 1998 provides only $400 million."

The 35-year-old span is federally owned, handles two-and-a-half times the traffic it was designed for, and is expected to last only five to seven more years, members of Congress at the hearing warned. The bridge services the Washington D.C. metropolitan area.

Panel Chairman Sen. John Warner said, "If we don't confront this, restrictions may be placed (on the bridge's use). It's too horrible to contemplate. It will have enormous economic repurcussions throughout the (region)," said the Virginia Republican.
But Jane Garvey, acting administrator for the Federal Highway Administration, said 1995 federal highway legislation does not require the federal government to kick in more than $400 million.
Moreover, the push for a balanced federal budget and heavy competition nationwide for U.S. transportation dollars restricts how much Washington can contribute, she said.

But Rep. Steny Hoyer, D-Md., noted that a coordinating committee set up to review the issue recommended a 12-lane drawbridge. "It is a pressing need for the Washington region and for the national transportation system," he said.
